result.title: FedQCal: Quadratic Programming with Dual-Space Calibration for One-Shot Federated Learning
result.summary: One-shot federated learning must combine heterogeneous client models after a single upload. Different local class distributions make it difficult to decide which client updates to retain. We propose FedQCal, which uses a reference model trained on a small labeled server set to define alignment requirements for aggregation. The key idea is to retain sufficient reference alignment while avoiding unnecessarily large aggregation coefficients. A minimum-norm quadratic program (QP) enforces these requirements. Classification loss on the same server examples selects a merge through two dual variables, so the alignment thresholds need not be prescribed in advance. We prove that the selected coefficients remain exact QP solutions at their induced thresholds. A perturbation bound explains how coefficient norm limits the amplification of projection errors. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN show gains over one-round FedAvg in most settings. Ablations support reference-guided weighting and coefficient calibration, even with one labeled server image per class.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 FedQCal：用服务器小规模标注集训练的参考模型给出对齐约束，通过最小范数二次规划选择客户端聚合系数，并借助对偶变量由分类损失确定阈值，附带精确性与扰动界分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「参考对齐约束 + 最小范数系数校准」思路可能启发多种 latent 假设或多路并行推理状态的加权合并与阈值设定，但论文不含视觉推理与内部状态环节，可供核查其权重分配与误差放大分析。
